newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SHARES OF SLOVAK VSZ LONG TERM BUY - ING.
newsitem.headline: SHARES OF SLOVAK VSZ LONG TERM BUY - ING.

text.p: Shares of VSZ a.s., the largest Slovak steel producer, remain a long-term buy after impressive first half earnings, an investor report issued by ING Barings said.

Its October investment report on Slovakia said it retained its LT-buy recommendation, as good company results showed the resilience of demand for flat steel, underpinned by growth in car production in Eastern Europe.
"The group (VSZ) is increasing the value added of its production and should continue to be a major beneficiary of growth in car sales in the region," the report said.
VSZ in July had posted a first half after-tax profit of 776 million crowns, compared to an after-tax profit of 650 million crowns in the same period in 1995.

ING Baring's said its recommendation was made on the share's price of 612 crowns on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE). VSZ closed at 650 crowns on the BSE on Friday, up 30 crowns, but on a thin volume of just 36 traded shares.
VSZ is a major supplier of the steel sheets to Czech car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s. and Volkswagen AG's Slovak unit Volkswagen Bratislava.

Earlier this month VSZ said it had started to discuss a possible increase in its exports of auto body sheets to the Russian car maker VAZ, which would increase VSZ exports to Russia to 100,000 tonnes a year from 60,000 tonnes.
VSZ has been a major supplier of steel to the German market for several years, and recently it has been in talks for the possible delivery of sheet metal for the German unit of Opel.
Last year VSZ supplied the state of Brandenburg with 111,000 tonnes of steel of which 78,260 tonnes went to the rolling mill Walzwerk Finnow.
ING Barings said VSZ was also continuing with its strategy of becoming a multi-national corporation, aiming to create a strong and integrated group of central European mills.
VSZ and Czech Trinecke Zelezarne (TZ) recently signed an agreement according to which VSZ may acquire 20 percent of TZ and TZ may acquire 10 percent of VSZ.

VSZ has been in talks aimed at to acquiring a 19 percent stake in the two largest Czech steel mills, Vitkovice and Nova Hut and has established contacts with Polish mill Huta Katowice, one of Poland's largest companies, ING Barings pointed out. -- Peter Javurek, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-210-3687
